en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man whose clothes fall upon a body of the deceased. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it (dead body) had been washed, so you would not wash whatever hits your clothes from it; and if it was so that it had not been washed, so wash whatever hits your clothes from it – meaning when the dead body is cold’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Ibrahim ibn al-Maymun who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man whose clothes fall on a dead body. He (the Imam) said, ‘If the dead body is given Ghusl (bath), then it is not necessary to wash such clothes, but if it is not given Ghusl (bath) yet, one must wash such clothes - and that is, when the dead body has become cold.’”
